title: Reduction of the rate of lymphatic fistula by intraoperative use of 4DryField®PH
summary:
Removal of the lymph nodes is often performed as part of the therapy for lymph node metastases. After surgery, a so-called lymphatic fistula is often formed with leakage of lymphatic fluid via the inserted drainage (this is a tube placed for the drainage of wound fluid). The postoperative lymphatic fistula rate is between 30-78.8% and up to 40% of patients suffer from chronic lymphedema (visible fluid accumulation in the intercellular spaces) after surgery.  

The purpose of this prospective, randomized, controlled study is to evaluate the effectiveness of 4DryField®PH in preventing the lymphatic fistula rate after lymph node dissection.
4DryField® PH is an already approved medical device for the prevention of adhesions/ adhesions and hemostasis. It consists of microparticles and is derived from potato starch. Due to the large surface area of the microparticles, 4DryField® PH extracts the fluid from the wound secretion. Cellular blood components and coagulation factors are concentrated and fibrin formation is promoted, thus encouraging adhesion of the wound and lymphatic channels. 4DryField® PH is degraded and completely absorbed by the body's own substances. The use of 4DryField®PH would be a low side effect and low cost strategy to prevent lymphatic fistulas after lymph node dissection.
This clinical trial is being conducted at the University Hospital of Bonn; a total of 178 patients are expected to participate. The study is funded by the Funding Instrument Clinical Studies (FKS) of the Commission for Clinical Studies at the University Hospital Bonn (UK Bonn).
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- The patient is at least 18 years old and at most 90 years old
- Written documented informed consent and agreement to participate in the study
- Patients who are able to follow study instructions and are likely to adhere to all required study visits (compliance)
- Patients who are scheduled for axillary or inguinal lymph node dissection
Exclusion criteria:
- Patient is unable to understand the scope, significance, and consequences of this clinical trial
- Known allergy to any of the components of the medical device
- Known or ongoing abuse of medications, drugs, or alcohol
- Lack of suitability of the patient to participate in the study as determined by the investigator
- Active disseminated coagulation disorder
- Patients with chronic lymphedema of the extremity to be operated on
- Emergency surgery
